# Declaration Clauses

> **Gap** GAP-DECLARATIONS-005

A struct or enum declaration may carry two clauses after its name, and a class keyword before `struct` or `enum`:

```metel
copy struct Point { x: i64, y: i64 }            // class keyword: one-word form of `derives Clone, Copy`
struct Pixel derives Clone, Copy { v: i64 }      // derives: the compiler writes the impls
declared aspect Validated;
struct Ticket: Validated { id: i64 }            // colon list: a user marker, an unchecked promise
struct Receipt: Validated derives Clone, Copy { id: i64 }   // both clauses, colon list first
```

The **colon list** names facts about the type that its declaration claims: a [`declared`](declaration-properties.md#spec.declarations.aspects.aspect-declaration-properties.legality-1)
aspect with no methods. A user marker is an unchecked promise, visible in the declaration. The **`derives` clause**
asks the compiler to write the impl of an aspect that has a derivation (`Copy`, `Clone`; the aspect declares it with the
`derivable` property, which only the standard library uses). `copy` before `struct` or `enum` is sugar for
`derives Clone, Copy`, and `linear` is reserved. Derivation is always explicit: a type with neither a `derives` entry nor
an `extend` of an aspect does not have it.

A generic type that derives a field-wise aspect has a **flow**: the type parameters the aspect depends on. A bare entry (`derives Clone`) and the `copy` class keyword state an empty flow, so the aspect holds for every argument. The argument list `(..)` (`derives Clone(..)`) asks the compiler to compute the flow from the fields, and a list of type parameters states it: `derives Copy(T)`, `derives Clone(A, B)`. The `copy` class keyword is unconditional and has no computed form: a type that is `Copy` only for some arguments writes the `derives` entries.

```metel
struct Wrapper<T> derives Clone(T), Copy(T) { value: T }           // Wrapper<X> is Copy exactly when X is
struct Pair<A, B> derives Clone(A, B), Copy(A, B) { a: A, b: B }   // `,` separates parameters and entries alike
copy struct View<T> { r: &T }                                        // no flow: Copy for every T
```

## The colon list

[A colon-list entry names a visible `declared` aspect with no methods and grants it to the type](#spec.declarations.aspects.declaration-clauses.legality-1); there is no negative entry.

<details>
<summary>Formal rules</summary>

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.aspects.declaration-clauses.legality-1}

A colon-list entry names a visible aspect that is `declared` and has no methods, and grants it to the type. An entry naming no aspect is an error. An aspect that has a derivation (`Copy`) is granted through `derives` or its class keyword instead, an aspect with methods through `derives` or `extend`, and an aspect that is not `declared` through `extend`; each is an error with a fix-it.

## The `derives` clause

[`derives A` is legal exactly when `A` has a derivation](#spec.declarations.aspects.declaration-clauses.legality-3), and a derived impl takes the place of a written one.

<details>
<summary>Formal rules</summary>

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.aspects.declaration-clauses.legality-3}

`derives A` is legal exactly when `A` has a derivation. An entry naming no aspect, or an aspect without a derivation, is an error.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 8156f9b70d40f62450255e0a8c9ce9c1af2d21b4 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.aspects.declaration-clauses.legality-4}

A derived impl and a written `extend` of the same aspect for one type overlap and are an error (`T0015`). A type customises an aspect by writing the impl instead of deriving it.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 8156f9b70d40f62450255e0a8c9ce9c1af2d21b4 -->

<!-- rfc.py:fixtures:start -->
<p class="rigor-backlink"><em>Tested by</em></p>
<details class="spec-fixture" data-fixture=""></details>
<!-- rfc.py:fixtures:end -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.aspects.declaration-clauses.legality-5}

The derived impl holds exactly when every field type has the aspect. A field type that does not is an error at the declaration, next to the field. For a generic type the flow says which type parameters must have the aspect: a bare entry states none, so a field whose aspect depends on a parameter is an error there, and with `(..)` the compiler computes the flow, which names a parameter only where a field's aspect depends on it. A parameter held only behind a shared reference, or only through a type whose own flow leaves it out, is not bounded. So `struct Wrapper<T> derives Clone(..), Copy(..)` is `Copy` exactly when `T` is, and `copy struct View<T> { r: &T }` is `Copy` for every `T`. A type declared inside a function body is solved with the other declarations of its block.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 7ff6bac2f3c159c0d57a74f61abbe3fcb3000089 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.aspects.declaration-clauses.legality-16}

For an aspect `E` with a super-aspect entry marked `derived B`, `derives E` requires that the same declaration derives `B` in its own entry, and so on transitively through `derived` entries of `B`. `copy struct` and `copy enum` count as `derives Clone, Copy`. A missing entry is an error that names the entry to add. A written `extend T: B` for a type whose declaration derives `E` is an error (`T0015`): delete the impl, or, when `E` can be written by hand, write `E` by hand too. `Copy` is granted only in the declaration, so for `Copy` the choices are to delete the written `Clone` or to drop `Copy`. The colon list cannot grant an aspect that has a derivation.

## The `copy` class keyword

[`copy` before `struct` or `enum` is `derives Clone, Copy`](#spec.declarations.aspects.declaration-clauses.legality-6), and derivation is idempotent per type and aspect.

<details>
<summary>Formal rules</summary>

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.aspects.declaration-clauses.legality-6}

`copy` before `struct` or `enum` is `derives Clone, Copy`, with no condition on the type parameters. The keyword has no conditional form: a type that is `Copy` only when its parameters are writes the `derives` entries, `derives Clone(..), Copy(..)` to compute the condition or `derives Clone(T), Copy(T)` to state it. The keyword takes no argument list and no `?`: `copy(T)`, `copy(A, B)`, `copy()` and `copy?` are errors whose message names those two forms. `linear` before `struct` or `enum` is reserved and is an error until linear types are implemented; it takes neither an argument list nor `?`.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 7ff6bac2f3c159c0d57a74f61abbe3fcb3000089 -->

<!-- rfc.py:origins:start -->
<span class="rigor-backlink">_Referenced by: [rfc-0206](../../../../rfcs/4-implemented/rfc-0206-copy-and-clone-sealed-implicit-copy.md), [rfc-0207](../../../../rfcs/4-implemented/rfc-0207-declaration-clauses-derives-and-the-colon-list.md), [rfc-0234](../../../../rfcs/4-implemented/rfc-0234-super-aspect-derivation-is-an-obligation.md), [rfc-0239](../../../../rfcs/4-implemented/rfc-0239-arguments-on-the-copy-class-keyword.md), [rfc-0244](../../../../rfcs/4-implemented/rfc-0244-unconditional-derivation-and-the-conditional-marker.md)_</span>

A `derives` entry for `Clone` or `Copy` in a declaration that has the `copy` class keyword restates an entry the keyword stands for, and the explicit entry replaces the keyword's, with its own mark: `copy struct H<T> derives Copy(T) { id: i64 }` keeps the keyword's unconditional `Clone` and states the `Copy` flow, and `pub copy struct W<T> derives Clone(T), Copy(T)` states both. A type whose `Clone` and `Copy` flows differ writes the `derives` entries.

## Derived `Clone` and `Copy`

[A derived `Clone` clones each field through that field's own `clone`](#spec.declarations.aspects.declaration-clauses.legality-8), and `Copy` requires it.

<details>
<summary>Formal rules</summary>

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.aspects.declaration-clauses.legality-8}

A derived `Clone` clones each field through that field's own `clone`; for an enum it keeps the active variant and clones its payload. A shared reference field is cloned by copying the reference. For a generic type the derived impl applies when each type parameter held by value in a field is `Clone`, so `struct View<T> { r: &T }` is `Clone` for every `T`.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 7ff6bac2f3c159c0d57a74f61abbe3fcb3000089 -->

<!-- rfc.py:fixtures:start -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.aspects.declaration-clauses.legality-9}

A derived `Clone` calls the field clones in a defined order: declaration order for a struct, and for an enum the payload fields of the active variant in declaration order. The clone of an anonymous record visits its fields in lexicographic label order. A panic in a field clone ends the program.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 8156f9b70d40f62450255e0a8c9ce9c1af2d21b4 -->

<!-- rfc.py:fixtures:start -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.aspects.declaration-clauses.legality-10}

`Copy` requires a derived `Clone` ([the obligation](#spec.declarations.aspects.declaration-clauses.legality-16)): a type that derives `Copy` also derives `Clone`, in its own entry, so `T: Copy` proves `T: Clone`. A written `extend T: Clone` for a type whose declaration derives `Copy` overlaps the derived one and is an error (`T0015`).

A type that derives `Copy` is `Clone` wherever it is `Copy`: the `Clone` flow must be contained in the `Copy` flow, so a larger stated `Clone` flow is an error at the `Copy` impl, naming the parameter. The derived `Clone` of a type at an instantiation where it is `Copy` is the representation copy, the same operation as the implicit copy of a use by value.

## Flow

[A `derives` entry for a field-wise aspect may state which type parameters the aspect depends on](#spec.declarations.aspects.declaration-clauses.legality-11); the compiler checks the stated flow or computes it.

<details>
<summary>Formal rules</summary>

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.aspects.declaration-clauses.legality-11}

An entry of a `derives` clause for a field-wise aspect (`Copy`, `Clone`) is written bare or followed by an argument list in parentheses: one or more type parameters of the declaration separated by commas, or the single entry `..`. The named parameters are the type's **flow** for that aspect: `N<A..>` has the aspect exactly when `N` derives it, the exclusions of the aspect hold at the instantiation, and every argument at a position in the flow has it. A bare entry states an empty flow and `(..)` is the flow the compiler computes ([flow of a bare or computed entry](#spec.declarations.aspects.declaration-clauses.legality-13)); `..` does not combine with named parameters, and a postfix `?` after an entry is an error that names `(..)`. The `copy` class keyword takes no list ([class keywords](#spec.declarations.aspects.declaration-clauses.legality-6)); its `?` is `derives Clone(..), Copy(..)`. An argument list on a derivation that takes none, on a negative entry, or naming something that is not a type parameter of the declaration is an error, and so is `(..)` on a derivation that is not field-wise, and so is the former `via` clause. A parameter of row or record kind is not accepted in the flow.

<!-- doc-example: expect-fail reason="the second declaration is the error the rule shows: `via` is replaced by the argument list" -->
```metel
struct Wrapper<T> derives Clone(T), Copy(T) { value: T }
struct Old<T> derives Copy via T { value: T }   // error: `via` is replaced by the argument list; write `derives Copy(T)`
```

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 7ff6bac2f3c159c0d57a74f61abbe3fcb3000089 -->

<!-- rfc.py:origins:start -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.aspects.declaration-clauses.legality-12}

The stated flow must contain every type parameter that a field's aspect depends on, and may contain more. The dependence of a field type is: a type parameter `P` depends on `{P}`; a nominal application `N<A..>` depends on the union of the dependences of its arguments at the positions in the flow set of `N`, and is an error at the field if `N` is not `Copy` for any arguments; a tuple or array depends on the union of its components; a reference and the `T[]` view depend on nothing; a primitive depends on nothing. A written function type is move-only, so a `Copy` type cannot hold one. A parameter missing from the stated flow is an error at the field, with a fix-it that adds it. A flow larger than needed is accepted and makes the type have the aspect only when those arguments do.

<!-- doc-example: expect-fail reason="the first declaration is the error the rule shows: `Copy(A)` does not cover `B`" -->
```metel
struct Bad<A, B> derives Clone(A, B), Copy(A) { a: A, b: B }   // error: field `b` depends on `B`, which `Copy(A)` does not cover
struct Handle<T> derives Clone(T), Copy(T) { id: i64 }   // accepted: Copy only when T is, whatever the fields become
```

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.aspects.declaration-clauses.legality-13}

A bare `derives` entry for a field-wise aspect, and the bare `copy` keyword, state an empty flow: every field's aspect must hold for every instantiation, and a field that depends on a type parameter is an error at the field, with a fix-it that names `(..)` and the computed set. An entry with `(..)` states the flow the compiler computes: the smallest set that satisfies the previous rule. A non-`pub` type may use `(..)`. A `pub` generic type may use `(..)` only when the computed set is empty; otherwise it is an error (`T0046`) with a fix-it that states the set, `derives Clone(T), Copy(T)`. An empty list (`derives Clone()`) is the bare entry. The stated or computed set is stored as the type's interface, and outside the defining module a client relies only on it.

<!-- doc-example: skip reason="the published binary predates the `(..)` entries; flip to expect-fail once it is released" -->
```metel
pub struct W<T> derives Clone(..), Copy(..) { value: T }   // error (T0046): a public generic type states its flow: `derives Clone(T)`
pub struct V<T> derives Clone(..), Copy(..) { r: &T }      // accepted: the computed flow is empty
```

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 8156f9b70d40f62450255e0a8c9ce9c1af2d21b4 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.aspects.declaration-clauses.legality-14}

The flow set describes a whole nominal type. A residual type `N<A..>.{ .f }` is `Copy` by the structural rule over its visible field types, whatever the flow set of `N` is. A `Copy` declaration with a field whose copy-ness depends on an associated type (`value: T::Item`) is an error, and so is one that depends on a parameter of row or record kind. A type that derives `Copy` has no negative grant of `Copy` and no `Drop` impl, conditional or not.

<!-- doc-example: expect-fail reason="the declaration is the error the rule shows: a field of associated type is rejected at its type" -->
```metel
aspect Source { type Item; }
copy struct Payload<T: Source> { value: T::Item }   // error: a Copy declaration cannot depend on an associated type
```

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 8156f9b70d40f62450255e0a8c9ce9c1af2d21b4 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.aspects.declaration-clauses.legality-15}

In a generic body, whether a value of a nominal type with a stored flow set is copied or moved is decided by the bounds in scope: it is copied exactly when every argument at a position in the flow set is known `Copy` (a type parameter by a bound that grants `Copy`, a nested application by its own flow set, a concrete type directly) and otherwise it moves, except that an argument at such a position that is itself undecided, a `dyn Aspect` whose erased type is not known to be `Copy` or not, leaves the ownership of the value undecided. That a value moves under the bounds in scope is not evidence that its type argument is not `Copy`: it does not select an implementation guarded by a negative bound, and for selection and coherence the fact stays undecided. The undecided-ownership diagnostic applies to a nominal type when it has no stored flow set, and to one with a stored flow set when an argument at a position in the flow set is undecided.

<!-- doc-example: expect-fail reason="`bad` is the error the example shows: `T` carries no `Copy` bound, so `w` moves" -->
```metel
struct Wrapper<T> derives Clone(T), Copy(T) { value: T }
fun twice<T: Copy>(w: Wrapper<T>) -> (Wrapper<T>, Wrapper<T>) { (w, w) }   // accepted
fun bad<T>(w: Wrapper<T>) -> (Wrapper<T>, Wrapper<T>) { (w, w) }           // error: use of moved value `w`
```
